title: The Flood Ward
premise: A river was buried in brick ninety years ago so a neighbourhood could be built on its bed; five weeks ago its water, its god and its demons came back up through the old tunnels, and the city sealed the Ward in behind a quarantine wall. Everyone inside has a plan for the source (bury it, harness it, give the river back, or blow the wall and walk away), and every plan needs the one man the demons listen to. When the failing Undergate finally gives way, the water has to go somewhere, and there isn't room for all of it.
theme: There isn't room for everything. Every position in the Ward makes room for one thing by pushing something else out: safety behind a wall, light that someone has to keep paying for, a river that was here first, people who'd rather be free than housed. Each is right about something, and each, pushed all the way, has a real cost. Refusing to choose is a position too: it helps no one, and the water chooses instead. Not law against chaos, not good against evil, and no secretly correct answer.

sources.source: Bunbuku Chagama, a Japanese folk tale (public domain): a tanuki turns himself into a teakettle, is sold, gets stuck half-changed, and earns money for the poor man who keeps him by doing tightrope tricks. Adapted: Bel is the keeper, and she is charging admission.

sources.what: The banshee's keening for a family
sources.source: Irish folklore (public domain): the bean sí keens for members of particular families before a death; she does not cause it. Adapted to the Ward's families, Haldane and Marchetti.

sources.what: The leprechaun's pot and his excuses
sources.source: Irish folklore (public domain): the shoemaker fairy with a crock of gold who escapes his captor by tricking him into looking away. Adapted into the privy ruse.

sources.what: Gonggong, the water god at the source
sources.source: Huainanzi, Shanhaijing and the Book of Documents (see src/data/demons/gonggong.json): the flood god who broke the pillar of heaven and was exiled by the sage kings. Adapted: a buried river's god, exiled again, under brick.

protagonist.who: An adult man (the player), gay, who rents the room over Bel's shop. No fixed backstory beyond this.
protagonist.why_him: On the first night of the rising he went down the storm drain after a neighbour's dog and came back up with the dog under one arm and a demon walking behind him, doing as it was told. Nobody else can talk to the things from the tunnels, so every faction needs him to carry its plan down.
protagonist.starts: Level 6, alone, in the Market Square in front of Bel's stall.

world: The Ward is an old low-lying district of the city built ninety years ago on the bed of the River Sallow, which was bricked into culverts underneath it.
Five weeks ago water and demons came up through the culverts. Three days later the city council sealed the Ward behind a concrete-and-wire quarantine wall. The council has no representative inside.
The council's terms are painted on the wall: the quarantine lifts when the hazard beneath the Ward is resolved. The ration drops stopped last Monday.
The Chapel Well on Chapel Hill is the Ward's only clean water. It is fed from below, by the buried river.
The Pumphouse has the only electric light this side of the canal, from an old turbine in the tunnels that Teo Marchetti got running again. He sells it by the hour.

The tunnels run down in three levels (the Culverts, the Cistern Galleries, the Undergate Approach) to the source: a cavern behind the Undergate, a ninety-year-old iron floodgate holding back what is left of the river.
Something at the source calls itself Gonggong, a god of floods. The demons in the tunnels came up with his water and answer to him the way flotsam answers a current.
Sump Row is the lowest street in the Ward, about two hundred people. It floods a little every spring. It sits exactly on the old riverbed.
Ines keeps two old blasting charges in the drain shed, left from when the locks were built. Two are enough to bring down the source chamber, or the base of the wall; one is not enough for either.
The only way down is the storm drain in the drain yard, south of the canal, through the drain shed.

factions.name: The Lockkeepers
factions.wants: Bring the roof down on the source with the charges and bury the river for good, so the council lifts the quarantine.
factions.cost: The Chapel Well dies with the source, and the Ward lives on council water at council prices, on council terms. Teo's turbine stops. Whatever is still down there is buried, including, if nobody finds him, Ines's own son.

factions.name: The Pumphouse
factions.wants: Beat the god and bind him with the Pumphouse Ledger to turn the Ward's turbines forever: light, clean water and work, with no need of the council.
factions.cost: The Undergate stays open by contract, so more demons come up every week to be put to work. The council never lifts the wall from a Ward full of bound demons. The Ward depends on a captive god, and on the man who holds his contract, who is the man who broke the gate.

factions.name: The Sallow Society
factions.wants: Give the river back its bed: let the god open the culverts and run the Sallow in daylight, and let the demons go home with it.
factions.cost: The river's bed is Sump Row. Two hundred people lose their homes, and the Ward is cut in two by a river nobody can wall in or out.

factions.name: The Wall Crew
factions.wants: Blow the council's wall with the charges and walk the whole Ward out together; the Ward is its people, not its streets, and the city can deal with its own buried river.
factions.cost: Whatever is in the tunnels walks out with them into a city that never wanted them, and no one is waiting on the other side. The Ward as a place ends. The old and the stubborn stay behind.

neutral.position: Stay behind the counter, sell to everyone, side with no one, be open when it's over.
neutral.cost: Helps no one. Bel is the living version of the High Water ending: she will be fine, and nothing she cares about will be saved by her.

facts.text: The River Sallow was bricked into culverts ninety years ago so the Ward could be built on its bed.
The Chapel Well is fed by the buried river. If the source is sealed, the well runs dry within a week.
The council has said the quarantine will lift once the hazard beneath the Ward is resolved. It has not said how it will judge that.
The Undergate will fail within days, whatever anyone does. The only question is where the water goes when it does.
There are two charges in the drain shed. Two can bring down the source chamber or the base of the wall. One can't do either.
Pell Haldane got out of the Ward before the wall went up and is waiting outside.
Pell Haldane is alive in the tunnels, trapped in the east gallery of the cistern with a broken leg.
Pell Haldane is home in the Ward with his mother, leg and all.
Pell Haldane is with you below, showing you the back way to the Undergate.
The Undergate gave way because it was old iron, ninety years of it. Nobody's fault.
Teo jammed the Undergate winch open with his own stamped wrench to run the turbine and sell power. That is what let the river and the demons up.
Teo's ledger binds only a god who has been beaten. Nobody signs standing up.
If the river gets its old bed back, it will only take the empty streets at the bottom of the Ward.
Sump Row sits exactly on the old riverbed. If the river comes back, it comes through Sump Row first: two hundred people.
Sump Row floods a little every spring. Nobody living there remembers why.
The demons came up with the river's water. They follow its god the way flotsam follows a current, and they would go back down with him.
The river's name, SALLOW, is carved on two old stones in the tunnels; the boundary marker was pulled out of one when the culverts were built.
Dario's sister has rooms and work lined up outside for everyone who comes out, and he talks to her on the radio every night.
The Wall Crew's radio died in the first week. No message has come through the wall since.
The old survey shows an outfall under the wall, bricked up ninety years ago.
There is a back way to the Undergate through the old shrine on the third level.
When the Undergate goes, Ines shuts the lower lock so the water stays below the Ward. She only does it when she is sure nobody is down there.

fixedEvents.what: Teo wedges the Undergate winch open to drive the turbine. The river's water, its god and its demons come up the culverts. Pell goes down to shut the gate and is trapped. Three days later the council seals the Ward.
The council's ration drops stop 'pending resolution'.

fixedEvents.when: the first time the player goes to the drain after meeting Ines, Teo and Dario (the shed stays padlocked until then)
fixedEvents.what: Dario's crew and Ines face off over the two charges at the drain shed. It always happens; the player decides how it ends: back Ines (she gives him both), back Dario (Dario takes both), split them (one each, so neither plan works yet), or walk past (Ines is knocked down and hurt, one charge goes in the canal, Dario's crew grabs the other).

fixedEvents.when: when the player first enters the Cistern Galleries, if Dario has a charge
fixedEvents.what: Dario blows one charge under the wall. The wall cracks and holds. The council floods the gap with floodlights and threatens force; a sealed storeroom cracks open in the Culverts. Happens only if Dario has a charge (backed him, split, or walked away).

fixedEvents.when: the end of the chapter, at the source, after Gonggong is beaten or lets the player pass
fixedEvents.what: The Undergate fails. This always happens. Who is where (Pell at home, beside the player, or still trapped; Dario at the wall with or without a charge; Sump Row warned or asleep), what the player carries (charges, ledger) and whom he has promised decide where the water goes and who pays for it. The player says in his own words what he does. When the gate goes, Ines shuts the lower lock behind him unless she knows someone is still below: if Pell is down there and nobody told her, the backwash nearly drowns him.

meters.mugs: How many times you tried to rob a demon in talk.
meters.trust_ines: How far Ines trusts you. Backing her at the shed (+2), promising to seal (+1, or +2 after asking about the well), bringing Pell home (+2); falls if you back Dario, give away her charges or walk past her.
meters.trust_teo: How far Teo trusts you. Taking his ledger (+1), keeping his secret (+1), opening his turbine intake (+1); falls if you expose him or warn Sump Row (his shift walks off).
meters.trust_hester: How far Hester trusts you. Promising to speak for the river (+1), kindness (+1), setting the stone back (+1), helping her face Sump Row (+1); falls if you open Teo's intake or tell her the river can't come home.
meters.trust_dario: How far Dario trusts you. Backing him at the shed (+2), promising to get everyone out (+1), flirting back (+1), giving him the charges below (+3) or your single charge (+2), warning Sump Row (+1), keeping his lie (+2); falls if you back Ines or refuse him.
meters.promises: How many factions you have explicitly promised to help (Ines, Teo, Hester, Dario). Three or more and every faction outcome closes: they will all act on your promise at once.
meters.talks: Conversations held with demons and people (engine-tracked).
meters.mercy: Demons you let go or that let you pass peacefully (engine-tracked).
meters.lies_caught: Lies you caught. Learning the truth isn't catching the lie; saying it to the liar's face is. Ines about Pell (proof: finding him; called at the Lock House once he's home, or in talk), Teo about the gate (proof: his wrench under the winch; called at the Pumphouse or in talk), Dario about his sister (proof: Bel's valves and the chalk radio log; called at the wall or in talk). Engine-tracked, and set by scenes.
meters.flirts: Times you flirted with a demon or a person (engine-tracked; saying 'Finish the line.' to Dario counts).
meters.outfit_talks: Talks you started while wearing armour that changes talking, like the Strappy Harness (engine-tracked).

finale.trigger: the Gonggong boss entity: after he is beaten or lets you pass, play finale_intro, then ask
finale.question: The Undergate is failing. What do you do?
finale.rule: Only outcomes whose requires are met are possible. The director reads the player's words and picks the closest possible outcome; if he asks for something his record makes impossible (for example sealing the source without the charges, or binding a god he didn't beat), it picks the nearest possible outcome and the narration shows why. If his words ask for something that is already too late (see tooLate), the narration says so, plainly and in the moment. Faction outcomes all require promises at most 2: a man who promised three or more factions can only end as Everybody's Man or High Water.

asides.asks: sending Pell home to his mother (he is with you at the gate)
asides.text: And Pell: you tell him to go home, and for once he doesn't argue. He takes the back way up at a limp, splint knocking on every step, to the one door in the Ward that has kept a lamp lit for him.

tooLate.asks: warning Sump Row, or getting people off the low street before the water comes
tooLate.text: Sump Row is three floors and a whole Ward away, and the gate has minutes. If anyone was going to knock on those doors, it had to happen before you came down.

tooLate.asks: blowing the roof or the wall with the single charge he carries
tooLate.text: One charge won't bring down the roof or the wall. Ines said so at the shed, and about charges Ines is never wrong. It makes a very loud noise and changes nothing.

tooLate.asks: setting off charges himself down at the gate (sealing the source, bringing the roof down) when Dario has the charges up at the wall; telling Dario to blow the wall is not this, that is the Breach
tooLate.text: You reach for charges you haven't got. They're up at the wall in Dario's hands, and the only thing you can send him from down here is your voice, up the drain.

tooLate.asks: blowing anything up, after he walked past the shed
tooLate.text: You have no charges. One went into the canal while Ines was on the cobbles, and Dario's crew spent the other on a crack in the wall.

tooLate.asks: getting everyone out of the tunnels first
tooLate.text: Somebody in the east gallery of the cistern was knocking on a pipe for three weeks. Nobody went to see who. There's no time to go back now.

outcomes.title: The Plug
outcomes.intent: Seal the source: plant the charges, bring the roof down, bury the river.
outcomes.ifUnmet: Without both charges there's nothing to seal it with. Without Ines's trust nobody up top closes the lower locks behind you. And a man who spent the whole descent refusing to kill anything finds his hand won't close on the plunger.
outcomes.narration: You wedge the charges into the Undergate's hinges and run. The roof comes down on the source with a sound you feel in your teeth, and the river goes back to being buried, under rock this time instead of brick. Within a week the Chapel Well runs dry, Teo's turbine stops, and the Ward drinks from council tankers at council prices. A month later the council takes down the wall and calls it a success; Ines stands at the gap and doesn't cheer. Whatever was still in the lower galleries is still there.
outcomes.verdict: You chose a wall you could trust over a river you couldn't, and paid for it in water.

He remembers the little fish who flirted with him at the gate. Gods have long memories, and nothing to do under rock but use them.

outcomes.title: The Engine
outcomes.intent: Bind the god: make the beaten Gonggong sign Teo's ledger and turn the turbines; harness the river for the Ward.
outcomes.ifUnmet: A god signs only on his back, and only for a man who knows how to keep demons working: without the ledger, without beating him, without a crew of your own and Teo's trust, the ink won't take.
outcomes.narration: Gonggong, on his back in the flood, signs Teo's ledger with a finger of river water, and the ink takes. By morning every turbine in the Ward is turning; there is light in Sump Row for the first time in five weeks and clean water from every tap. The Undergate stays open by contract, and every week a few more demons come up it and are put to work hauling, lighting, pumping. The council looks at a Ward full of bound demons and adds a second ring of wire to the wall. Teo is the most important man in the Ward now, and he makes sure everyone knows who brought him the god.
outcomes.verdict: You chose a light that someone has to keep paying for, and let the man who broke the gate hold the bill.

Pays Teo for light like everyone else, and puts her prices up to match.
A god in harness. Patient. Contracts end.
He signed on his back and held your eye the whole time, as if lying there had been his idea. Teo cleared his throat.

outcomes.title: The River Comes Home
outcomes.intent: Give the river back: let Gonggong take his old bed, open the culverts, let the Sallow run in daylight and the demons go home.
outcomes.ifUnmet: The god only takes his river home gently for a man who spoke to him instead of beating him, who spared some of his children on the way down, and whom Hester's people trust enough to pull up the culvert grates.
outcomes.narration: You stand aside, and Gonggong takes the gate in his coils and opens it like a door. The Sallow comes up its old bed under the Ward, lifting the culverts out of the ground brick by brick, and by dawn it runs in daylight for the first time in ninety years, straight down Sump Row. The wall breaks where the river crosses it, and no council on earth can wall up a river; the demons go back into the water with their god. Sump Row is gone. The Ward is two halves now, with a river between them.
outcomes.verdict: You gave the river back its room, and took it from the people who were living there.

fates.text: Stands on the new bank and weeps, for both reasons.
Runs the relief kitchen on Chapel Hill for a month, sleeves rolled up, counting every family twice.
Everyone got out, two hundred and six, because Hester went up and counted them twice. They lost everything they couldn't carry up the hill.
Everyone got out: Pell knocked on every door on his way home. They lost everything they couldn't carry up the hill.
Everyone got out. They lost everything they couldn't carry up the hill.
Nobody had knocked on Sump Row's doors, and by the time the water was in the street it was too late to start. The man who swept his step every morning is never found.
Her locks are under ten feet of river. She leaves the Ward with Pell carrying her bag, and doesn't look back.
Her locks are under ten feet of river. She leaves the Ward.
Her locks are under ten feet of river. She leaves the Ward with Pell carrying her bag, and doesn't look back.

Her locks are under ten feet of river. Pell came up out of the cistern beside you, soaked from the lock she'd shut on him, and that was how she learned he'd been below. She leaves the Ward with him carrying her bag, and never asks why you didn't tell her.
You'd promised her the source. She tells Chapel Hill so, once, in the voice she uses for the weather.
The turbine hall floods; the Pumphouse is a shell. He sells candles, and the people who know who wedged the gate buy theirs from Bel.
The turbine hall floods; the Pumphouse is a shell. He sells candles.
His crew walks out through the gap the river made. Half of them walk back. The ones who knew nobody was waiting keep going.
His crew walks out through the gap the river made. Half of them walk back.
He got his nan and her budgie up Chapel Hill the night before, because you sent him. He stands on the new bank and watches the river take her street.
You backed him at the shed, and he hasn't forgotten it. He's first through the gap the river made, and he waits on the far side for you, longer than he needs to.
He promised you a better line once he got out. A river got him out, which he says counts. The line is still terrible. You let him finish it.
Watches the river come up Sump Row from his mother's step on Chapel Hill, and knocks on the doorframe three times, for luck.
Comes up out of the cistern beside you, soaked to the neck, laughing like a man who has stopped being anybody's excuse.
Went up the back way when you told him to, and watched the river come up Sump Row from his mother's step.
The river carries him up into the daylight half-drowned and puts him down on the new bank.
By the end of the week she's selling boats. Of course she is.
He tips his head to you as he goes, once. From a god, that is a great deal.
The second time, he winks.

outcomes.title: The Breach
outcomes.intent: Break out: send the flood at the wall, let Dario blow it, walk the whole Ward out with the water.
outcomes.ifUnmet: Dario needs a charge in his hand and a reason to believe you; and a man who ran from every fight down there doesn't get followed through a hole in a wall.
outcomes.narration: You turn the flood down the old culvert towards the wall and shout up the drain, and up in the Ward Dario lights the fuse. The wall goes out in one long breath of concrete and water, and the whole Ward walks out through the gap with the flood around its ankles: old men, kids, cats in boxes, demons. The council's lines break; nobody can hold a wall that isn't there. On the other side is a city that never wanted them, and no one is waiting with rooms. The Ward as a place is over; the Ward as people walks on into the city, together, for now.
outcomes.verdict: You chose the people over the place, and found out how much of them was the place.

fates.text: He keeps looking for his sister in a crowd she isn't in. The people he lied to don't forgive him for weeks.
He keeps looking for his sister in a crowd she isn't in. The people he lied to don't forgive him for weeks.
He keeps looking for his sister in a crowd she isn't in. When the crew works out nobody was ever waiting, they forgive him inside a week. You knew, and walked them out anyway. That takes them longer.
He keeps looking for his sister in a crowd she isn't in, and keeps the story going because you told him to. You're the only one who knows not to ask him how she is.
They came knowing nobody was waiting. That is worth more to him than he can say, and he tries to say it to you anyway.
You backed him at the drain shed, in front of everyone. On the far side of the wall he tells that story to anyone who'll stand still, and you get a little taller every time.
He promised you a better line once he got out. He's out. It takes him three days to write, it's terrible, and you let him say the whole thing.
Somebody has to keep the locks. She's still there when the water goes down.
Pell carries her bag. She doesn't look back at the Lock House, which is how you know it costs her.
Pell carries her bag. She doesn't look back at the Lock House, which is how you know it costs her.

She learned Pell had been below the whole time when he walked up out of the drain beside you, soaked from the lock she'd shut. Somebody has to keep the locks. She stays, and watches him walk out without her.
You promised her the source. She heard the wall go instead, and knew which of your promises you'd kept.
Loads his generator on a cart and sells light to the refugees at a fair price, for once.
Loads his generator on a cart and sells light to the refugees at a fair price, for once. The ones who know he wedged the gate pay anyway, and don't say thank you.
Goes back down to the river alone.
Walks out through the breach with his mother's bag on his shoulder, his splint knocking on the broken concrete.
Walks out through the breach on his broom-handle splint, last of all, knocking on the broken wall as he goes.
Went home when you told him to, and walked out through the breach with his mother's bag on his shoulder.
The flood carries him out through the breach. He finds the Ward empty and his mother gone ahead.
Walks out through the breach together, straight off Chapel Hill, carrying what it had already packed.
Wakes to the flood running under its doors on the way to the wall, and runs with it. Most of them make the gap.
Stays open. Somebody has to be, when they come back. Some of them do.
His river runs out into the city's drains. He follows it.
He'll find you out there. He said so, in the voice he saved for when you flirted with him.

outcomes.title: Everybody's Man
outcomes.intent: Try to give everyone something: a compromise, a channel for the river, the pumps kept, the wall opened, all at once; or simply having promised everyone.
outcomes.narration: Everyone acts on what you told them, at the same moment. Ines's people slam the lower locks shut, Teo throws every turbine lever open, Dario's crew is at the wall with whatever they have, and Hester's people haul up the culvert grates to let the river through. The water has four places to go and goes to all of them badly: the turbine hall floods and collapses, the locks burst, Sump Row goes under, and the wall holds. By morning nobody has what they wanted, everybody has lost something, and every one of them remembers that you promised. Somewhere in the cistern, a god is laughing.
outcomes.verdict: You tried to give everyone a yes, and the water held you to every one of them.

fates.text: Caught in the lower lock when it burst. She lives. She doesn't speak to you.
Nobody had told her Pell was below. She found out when you brought him up out of the cistern, and added it to the list.
You'd promised her the source. She heard you promise the others too.
The turbine hall is rubble. He tells everyone whose idea it was.
The wall held. His crew scattered. He waits for you to explain, and you can't.
You backed him at the shed, out loud, in front of everyone. That's the part he can't get past: you were on his side, and on everyone else's too.
He'd promised you a better line when he got out. He doesn't get out. He never brings it up, and neither do you.
Sits on the drowned grate on Sump Row with her notebook shut.
Goes under, the way everyone promised it wouldn't. Nobody drowns: they were up on Chapel Hill, because somebody told them in time.
Goes under in the night. Not everyone gets out.
Hauls his mother out of the burst lock on his bad leg. He doesn't ask whose idea it was. He knows.
Stands beside you in the cistern while four kinds of water come at once. 'Well,' he says. 'You tried.'
Went up the back way when you told him to, which is the only reason he was there to haul his mother out of the burst lock.
Still in the east gallery when four kinds of water came at once.
Sells to all of them the next morning. 'Told you, love.'
Laughing in the cistern. He'll be back.
When he comes back, he says, he'll ask for you by name.

outcomes.title: High Water
outcomes.intent: Fallback. Waiting, hesitating, refusing to choose, walking away to save himself, or asking for something his record makes impossible.
outcomes.narration: You don't choose, so the water does. The Undergate fails on its own and the river takes the lowest road it can find: the Pumphouse floods to the rafters, Sump Row goes under to the windowsills, and the wall holds. Nobody's plan happens; nobody's plan is stopped, either. The council sends pumps a week later and keeps the wall up another year to be sure. Everyone in the Ward remembers that you were the one standing in front of the gate.
outcomes.verdict: You kept every door open until the water closed them.

fates.text: Waits for the council's next terms. She's good at waiting. She hates it.
Pell climbed out of the tunnels beside you, soaked from the lock she'd shut on him, and that was how she found out he'd been below. She doesn't ask why you never told her.
You promised her you'd seal it. Then you stood in front of the gate and didn't.
Pumps out the Pumphouse and starts again, smaller.
Keeps chipping at the wall.
Keeps chipping at the wall, and keeps telling everyone his sister is waiting.
You backed him at the shed, then stood still at the gate. He isn't angry. He just stops saving you a place by the wall.
He still owes you a better line. He says he's saving it for the day the wall comes down, and you both pretend that's soon.
Stays down in the culverts with her stone, talking to the river, which isn't listening.
Spends the week after the flood on Sump Row with a mop and a clipboard, counting.
Goes under to the windowsills while its people watch from Chapel Hill. They come back down to mud, and to each other.
Goes under to the windowsills in the night. Most get out through the upstairs windows. Not all.
Home, limping, and the only Haldane who'll talk to you about any of it.
Climbs out of the tunnels beside you. 'Well,' he says, 'that's one way to decide.'
Went home when you told him to: the only Haldane who'll talk to you about any of it.
The council's pump crews find him a week later, alive, just.
Still open. 'Somebody has to be.'
Half his river is in the Ward's cellars now. He is in no hurry.
Some nights the water in your cellar is warm. You decide not to think about why.

reflections.text: You went down in a harness instead of armour and flirted with half of what came up out of the river. It got you further than armour would have. It also got you bitten.
You went down dressed for the conversation, not the fight. It opened mouths that armour would have kept shut, and let a few of them bite. A body can only wear so much at once.

You flirted your way down through the flood: with demons, with anything else that would hold still, and with Dario, who'd had exactly one line and spent it on you. Being wanted is a kind of protection. It just isn't the kind that stops teeth.
You flirted with nearly everything that came up out of the river, and never once with Dario, who'd have blushed for you. Being wanted is a kind of protection. It just isn't the kind that stops teeth.
You never flirted back, not with the demons and not with Dario, who tried. You kept that part of yourself out of the flood. It stayed dry. It also stayed shut.
You caught all three of them lying, Ines, Teo and Dario, and said so to their faces. It never made choosing easier. It only meant that whatever you chose, you chose it knowing.
Everyone lied to you a little, and you never once called them on it. That's not a crime. It's how most people get through a flood.

Teo's was the first door you knocked on, and you stood under the winch he wedged open and never put it to him. He'd have told you everything for the asking. Friends get the first cup and the last word.
You stood under the winch Teo wedged open and never put it to him. He'd have told you everything for the asking. He's still telling the Ward it was old iron.

You found Ines's son alive, kept him below with you, and let her go on telling the Ward that nobody was down there. When the gate went she shut the lower lock on him with a clear conscience. You were the only one who could have told her.
You found Ines's son alive and never made her say she'd lied about him. That was kind, and she knows it. The next time she tells the Ward something is safe, they'll believe her, and so will she.
You knew Dario's radio was dead and let him go on chalking messages from his sister on the wall. Some lies hold a crew together. You never asked which kind his was.
You knew Dario's radio was dead and let him go on chalking messages from his sister on the wall. Some lies hold a crew together. You never asked which kind his was.
You never went looking for the knocking. Somebody down there was counting days.
At the drain shed you stepped past and let them sort it out. Ines's wrist remembers.
At the drain shed you cut the difference, and handed two people half a bridge each.
You went to Dario before anyone else, and then at the drain shed you picked Ines, out loud, in front of him. He'd have followed you anywhere. You made him watch you go the other way.
At the drain shed you picked Ines, early and out loud, in front of a boy who'd have followed you anywhere.

The Lock House was the first door you knocked on, and then at the drain shed you made Ines hand her charges to Dario in front of everyone. She'd taken that first knock as a promise. You never said it wasn't one.
At the drain shed you picked Dario, early and out loud, in front of a woman who'd kept the water off your street for thirty years.
You said yes to almost everyone. It felt like kindness at the time.
You never promised anyone anything. Nobody could hold you to it, and nobody could count on you.
You talked to everything that would listen, human or not. Words got you further down than swords would have. Up here, people call that stalling.
You killed a great many of the things that came up with the water. Somebody had to. You never asked who decided that.
You barely raised a hand to anything down there. You came up with a crew instead, and nobody in the Ward could tell any more whose side they were on.
When a demon wouldn't give you what you wanted, you took it. That's one way to make room for yourself: there's always somebody with less afterwards.
You let a lot of them walk away. Mercy is a position too. It costs whoever they walk into next.
You ran when it went bad, more than once. Running keeps every option open. So does standing still.
You caught people lying to you, and it didn't make choosing any easier. The truth almost never does.

coda: Every plan in the Ward was a way of choosing what to make room for: the wall, the light, the river, the people. Each of them was right about something. Each of them, pushed all the way, pushed something else out.
So did you. That was always going to be the price of standing in front of the gate.

objectives.text: Ines Haldane wants a word before you go down. She's in front of the Lock House, west of the square.
Teo Marchetti wants a word before you go down. He's at the Pumphouse, east of the square.
Dario Venn wants a word before you go down. He's at the wall, south-east, over the east bridge.
The way down is the drain shed, over the middle bridge. Ines has the key, and Dario's crew is waiting for her.
Dario's radio has been dead since the first week, and he's still telling the Wall Crew somebody is waiting.
Dario's test blast cracked the wall. The single charge you carry is the other half of what he needs.
Something in the Cistern keeps knocking, three at a time, from somewhere east.
Sump Row doesn't know the survey's numbers yet. Somebody has to tell two hundred people to get up the hill.
Hester still thinks the river's old bed is empty streets. She's at the Sallow shrine in the Culverts.
Pell went up to the Ward. Ines will want to know you found him.
You've seen the Undergate winch. Teo still tells everyone the gate gave because it was old iron.
Hester's Sallow Stone has a twin somewhere deeper, with an empty socket in its face.

engineNotes: Conditions everywhere use the engine's meets() format: { flags: { f: true|false }, meters: { m: { min, max } } }. An unset flag counts as false; meters start at 0.
Map entities use showIf for conditional visibility (alternatives may share a tile when their showIf conditions exclude each other). Triggers use requires. Stairs use toX/toY.

NEW entity type 'demon' (ward kettle, culvert leprechaun, cistern Furfur, south-hall banshee): a visible, blocking, fixed demon. Bump: play its scene once, then open the normal demon talk/fight encounter with that demon at that level (talk can end in join, leave, pass, gift or a fight; escape allowed). Any resolution sets its flag (each has showIf flag false, so it disappears). talkNote is extra direction for this encounter, appended to the demon's card in the talk prompt. Optional leftFlag: set only when he walks off (left, passed, fled, or you walked away), not when he joins or is beaten. A demon above your level that you only talked to stays on the map.

Boss entity: flag (set on any resolution), winFlag 'gonggong_beaten' (set only if he is beaten in battle; the_engine and river_home depend on it), talkFlag 'gonggong_heard' (set if talk ends peacefully), talkNote (as for demon entities), after 'finale_intro', finale true.

Scene choices may carry give (item id added to inventory), take (item id removed) and learn (fact ids added to story.facts, so NPC lies with truthFact can be caught in free talk). Flags carry all story logic; the items are for the inventory and flavour.

Scene choices may also carry record (a short second-person past-tense line, e.g. 'You backed Dario at the drain shed.'; the Journal's 'What you've done', NPCs and the director see only these, so every real decision has one and filler like 'Keep going.' has none) and heal (full HP/MP for the party). Lies are never caught by a reveal scene: a reveal teaches the truth fact (and sets a knows_* flag), and the catch is the player saying so, in free talk or in a confrontation choice that sets caught_<npc>_<about> and lies_caught +1.
Speakers that are not NPC names: 'Kettle' (tanuki), 'Leprechaun', 'Furfur', 'Banshee', 'Gonggong' (demon portraits).

Outcome extra fields for the director: intent (what the player has to say to aim at it), ifUnmet (why it is impossible when its requires fail), verdict (one-line SMT I-style judgment). Show the matching reflections (requires met, up to three) and the coda after the narration.
Narrations and the coda never say 'End of the prologue.'; the ending screen shows endText once, as its footer. A fate's who is an NPC id, a demon id, or a plain display name (e.g. 'Sump Row').

objectives: [{ id, text, where, showIf?, doneIf }]. Active = showIf met (or absent) and doneIf not met. where is the map id the loose end is tied up on, so the engine can say when one points back up. List order is story order; the last active one is the most recent.

finale.tooLate: [{ id, asks, keywords, when, text }]. Entries whose when is met are things the player can no longer do. Give them to the director; if the player's words ask for one (the mock director: any keyword in his words), the narration includes its text.
Facts may carry supersedes: [fact ids]. Once the player has learned the newer fact, the Journal hides or strikes the older ones (a lie's false fact is superseded by the truth that catches it).

Every scene choice has next: a scene whose first line is the other speaker's (or the world's) reaction. Scenes reached from several triggers set a flag the triggers require to be false, so they can't repeat.

Shop entities may sit below ground: { name, keeper (demon id, for the portrait), sprite, scene (played once, the first time, before the shop opens), stock (item ids; default Bel's list), priceMult (default 1), armor (true: armor section shown, so owned armor can be swapped there) }.

Boss talkMood: [{ requires, mood, note }]. When the boss talk starts, add each met entry's mood to his starting mood and append its note to the talk context ('Right now: ...'), so what the player showed or told him at the gate (the gg_* flags from gonggong_meet) and his record count, and gold alone doesn't.
